Player surface / context: Canvas-first reusable controls used by videos/games and partially by music
Media model: Separate video/audio elements; shared playbackRates [0.5,0.75,1,1.25,1.5,2]; assetUrl path resolution; optional PLL-style syncAudioToVideo
Controls exposed to user: Play/pause; seek; set volume; toggle mute; playback rate; optional back/exit; control visibility animation
Settings / state authority: localStorage keys site.audio.allowed, site.audio.volume, site.audio.muted, site.audio.sync
Similarities to others: Videos and Games already depend on this; Music reuses shared helpers but wraps them in page-specific logic
UX strengths to keep: Best existing foundation for a unified player engine; already handles rate, mute, volume, seek, buffered-state heuristics, and sync smoothing

Recommendation for source of truth: Use this as the technical base layer only. Split it into engine, adapter, and skin. Do not let page-specific paths or page-specific UX stay in the core.

Player surface / context: Hero 3D tablet with intro animation, gate, skip button, then thumbnail-driven reel playback on the tablet/screen
Media model: HQ/LQ videos plus separate opus audio tracks and thumbnails; intro video plus intro audio; tablet pose persistence
Controls exposed to user: Intro play gate; progress/load bar; skip intro; shared canvas controls; play/pause; seek; mute; volume; playback rate; fullscreen-ish expanded playback; thumbnail selection
Settings / state authority: Reads and writes global audio sync and mute/volume via localStorage; also stores videosPage_tabletPose
Similarities to others: Uses shared engine most directly; adapter pattern already present
UX strengths to keep: Keep the intro gate/load state, skip behavior, and the thumbnail-to-full-play transition. Best example of onboarding users into a media experience.
UX weaknesses / risks: Complex bootstrap and many moving parts; intro logic is heavy; pathing fragile; a lot of UX is tightly coupled to the 3D scene lifecycle
Recommendation for source of truth: Best candidate for the reference content-player flow. Keep its reel browsing, preview-to-play transition, and adapter pattern, but simplify intro orchestration.

Player surface / context: Arcade cabinet screen that switches between game iframe content and reel/sample video content
Media model: Mixed-content screen: iframe game modes, HQ/LQ webm videos, separate opus audio, splash images, thumbnails
Controls exposed to user: Shared canvas controls when in video mode; play/pause; seek; mute; volume; playback rate; exit/back; game audio bridging

Similarities to others: Reuses shared player engine and adapter idea from videos

Player surface / context: Two distinct experiences: small decorative tablet player and a more bespoke top-pad / track video player embedded in the instrument UI
Media model: Multiple synchronized systems: audio playback, HQ/LQ track videos, tablet thumbnail/video loop, MIDI timing, soundfonts, custom backboard/canvas UI
Controls exposed to user: Shared controls for track video plus page-specific actions; play/stop; playback rate; mute; sync slider; keyboard shortcuts; tablet mini-player with centered play button; instrument and grid toggles intermixed with media controls
Settings / state authority: Uses global sync store via global-sync.js and shared site.audio keys, but also adds page-specific transport and MIDI timing state
Similarities to others: Reuses shared controls and sync helpers, but wraps them in a very custom music-specific transport
UX strengths to keep: Keep the sync slider, keyboard shortcuts, and the way the player integrates with the page's primary task instead of feeling bolted on. Strongest advanced-user control surface.
UX weaknesses / risks: Most complex and least reusable player UX because media controls are intertwined with instrument, MIDI, and visualization logic; there are effectively two players on one page
Recommendation for source of truth: Do not use this page as the baseline whole-cloth. Cherry-pick advanced controls only: sync slider, keyboard shortcuts, and transport feedback. Keep the decorative tablet player separate from the main source-of-truth player.

Media model: Single engine should support separate video/audio, thumbnails, optional intro state, and non-video content adapters
Controls exposed to user: Core controls should be play/pause, seek, mute, volume, playback rate, exit/back, and optional sync slider; advanced features should be opt-in
Settings / state authority: Global authority should own permission, master volume, muted state, and audio sync offset
Similarities to others: Videos and Games prove the engine/adapter approach; Start proves the global settings model; Music proves the need for advanced optional controls

UX weaknesses / risks: Avoid: page-specific paths in shared code, duplicated localStorage logic, decorative mini-players pretending to be the main player, media logic mixed directly into scene bootstrapping
Recommendation for source of truth: Source of truth should be: shared engine from shared-video-controls/video-player-controls, global settings model from start/index, page adapter pattern from videos/games, and optional advanced controls from music.
